items.title: Alton Purnell Interview, 1968-03-03
items.q: See, Bunk hired the George Lewis band, which we all played together, and he was just a new man in the band. And so when Bunk came in and accepted our band to play with him, then they named it Bunk Johnson's band.

ctx.x: I'll get one from him before we quit. Alton, I've heard a lot of your records going way back, I think. I don't know whether you ever played with Oliver on Snagit, of which I've got a copy at home, but I'm sure you were back in there somewhere.
No, I didn't play with Oliver, but I made Snagit with Bunk Johnson, which is one of the old trumpet players around Oliver's age, you know.

Well, Bunk Johnson, if I remember correctly, the records I've got of his, he made with Lou Waters up at Hambone Kelly some years ago after they rediscovered Bunk. You know, they found him pitching cotton or something. I don't know what he was doing, but they brought him a new set of teeth and brought him a trumpet, and away we went.

items.title: Alton Purnell Interview, 1958-08-29
items.q: When I went to New York with Bunk's band, Bill, I could have made more money playing with Smiling Joe.

ctx.x: You know. Well we're getting near the end of this. Is there anything else you'd like to add on here? Well. Well. Well. I.

I just like to add that I like the jazz. When I went to New York with Bunk's band, Bill, I could have made more money playing with Smiling Joe. But I like the jazz so much that I'd rather be with them. And right now, Bill, I think that George Lewis who has the band, has one of the greatest authentic jazz bands that ever live in. And that there will never be another band like his after those minutes have passed. Well they got on record a lot of times. A lot of people have heard you all over the world.
Yeah. So that last part of his career, so the last few years is well recorded there too. Yeah, I made a lot of recording with them and I sure miss them, Bill.
